correctness.rationale: Pair merging iff synchronization for all pairs is proved by iterative subset compression; the length recurrence is exact via first-letter analysis. Two independent exhaustive algorithms (reverse BFS and synchronous fixed point) both examine all 9,765,625 ordered labeled five-state transition pairs and reproduce exactly the same 8,063,385 sync total and threshold counts [3,444,345,3,763,200,738,000,108,720,9,120]. Canonicalization over all 120 state permutations and two letter orders yields 38 classes, each independently reconstructed as a 240-element orbit with disjoint union equal to all 9,120 extremizers. Python separately checks representative word lengths and each extremizer’s strong connectivity and map ranks. No infinite-domain extrapolation.

value.rationale: The prescribed-state compress-with-another quantity is singled out by a recent 2026 survey of difficult synchronization bounds. The claim gives a complete finite benchmark on the entire 9,765,625-element binary five-state transition universe, not just a sample or routine checking a single automaton: all possible exact values and multiplicities, sharp maximum, complete 38-orbit extremal classification, the fact every extremizer is strongly connected, and rank-type stratification. These structural quantities are not implied by neighboring avoidance/triple-rendezvous tables and provide an exact benchmark for proposed general bounds.
